result.title: Vision-Language Truck Driving Advisories Grounded in Provincial Rules and Forecast Risks
result.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures. This manuscript has been submitted to the 38th IEEE Intelligent Vehicles Symposium (IV 2027)
result.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) can generate context-aware driving advisories, but their outputs may conflict with road conditions or traffic rules, and they typically address a hazard only once it is visible. This matters for long-haul trucking, where heavy trucks need long stopping distances and a single trip may cross several jurisdictions with different traffic regulations. This paper proposes a data generation and distillation framework that integrates structured scene understanding, risk forecasting, and traffic-rule retrieval to generate truck driving decisions and natural-language advisories, with a consistency check on every record. The records, written by an 8B teacher, are then used to distill a 3B-parameter student model for onboard deployment. We also introduce a dashcam dataset covering four Canadian provinces, comprising 11,142 annotated lane-marking frames and 9,494 driving segments. On held-out driving data across all four provinces, the student passes the consistency check in 94.6% of the segments, against 20.2% for the untuned 8B teacher, and announces 26.2% of the risks in the next 10 to 30 seconds before they appear. Of the generated advisories, 97.7% conform to the provincial traffic rules and guidance. These findings suggest that the framework can produce rule-conforming training data for compact driving advisory models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出面向长途卡车的驾驶建议数据生成与蒸馏框架：整合结构化场景理解、风险预测与省级交通规则检索，由 8B 教师模型生成决策及自然语言提示并对每条记录做一致性校验，再蒸馏为 3B 学生模型，同时发布加拿大四省行车数据集。
AI.relevance_reason: 逐条一致性校验筛选教师输出后再蒸馏的流程，可供核查是否能用于 LVR 轨迹训练的监督过滤与验证；但论文本体是驾驶提示的任务应用，未涉及 latent 推理状态，迁移线索有限。
